newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Airlines report strong passenger traffic growth.
newsitem.headline: Airlines report strong passenger traffic growth.

text.p: World airlines on Thursday reported strong growth in international passenger traffic of nine percent in the first four months of 1997 over a year ago.

The increase in seat supply in the same period was smaller, at six percent, the global airlines body, the International Air Transport Association (IATA), said in a statement. Passenger traffic grew nine percent in April over a year ago.
Global air freight traffic growth was nearly 10 percent in the first four months of 1997 over a year ago and nine percent in April, an IATA statement added.
The growth in total air traffic, which includes passengers and freight, was 9.2 percent in January-April over the same 1996 period against a total capacity increase of 5.5 percent.
The statement gave no breakdown for growth in regions.
Industry figures show that a total of 2.5 billion people passed through the world's airports in 1996, partly thanks to a steady worldwide growth in leisure travel.

The emerging economies of the Asia-Pacific region led the upward surge last year. IATA says the region's air passenger traffic, with a 35 percent global share, is expected to soar to nearly 50 percent by 2010 or to 393 million passengers, nearly triple the present volume.
